## Introduction

In Module 1 we gave each nucleus a continuous score for every reference
phenotype. Within cardiomyocytes, those scores already *hint* at a
foetal→adult gradient. Module 2 turns that hint into a single number per
cell: **pseudotime**.

High-throughput sequencing 

Pseudotime orders cells so that cells close together in a biological
process get close values. It is not real time, and its scale is
arbitrary: only the *ordering* matters. Which end counts as "early" is a
separate choice, and for some methods it has to be supplied. Here the
Φ-Space `fetal` score tells us where maturation starts.



### Three ways to order cardiomyocytes

We compute three pseudotimes, all from the Φ-Space scores:

1. **Φ-Space pseudotime:** the adult-like score minus the foetal score.
   No trajectory model at all; this is our baseline.
2. **Slingshot,** a *principal-curve* method. It clusters cells, links
   the cluster centres into a tree, fits a smooth curve through it, and
   projects every cell onto the curve. Pseudotime is the distance along
   the curve.
3. **Diffusion pseudotime (DPT)** with the destiny package. It builds a
   graph of similar cells and measures how far a random walk travels
   from a root cell.

We then check them against each other and against the donors' ages,
which none of the methods sees. Finally, we look at a common pitfall:
slingshot's answer depends on how you cluster the cells.

A **Going further** section at the end repeats the analysis on a PCA
embedding of gene expression instead of Φ-Space, for anyone who wants to
compare.


## Load Libraries and Module 1 Output

```{r load-libraries}
library(SingleCellExperiment)
library(slingshot)
library(destiny)
library(scater)
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(tibble)
library(patchwork)
library(RColorBrewer)
```

Module 1 handed over a single file: the query with Φ-Space scores in
`reducedDim`, scran logcounts in `assay(query, "logcounts")`, and the
per-cell annotations (`PhiCellType`, `PhiCellTypeBroad`, `PhiAge`,
`group`, …) in `colData`.

```{r load-module1}
query <- readRDS(file.path(results_dir, "05_phispace_query.rds"))

cat("Assays:      ", paste(assayNames(query), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("reducedDims: ", paste(reducedDimNames(query), collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Cells:       ", ncol(query), "\n")
cat("Broad types: ", paste(sort(unique(query$PhiCellTypeBroad)),
                            collapse = ", "), "\n")
```

```{r cache-setup}
results_dir <- Sys.getenv("SCW_RESULTS", "../results")
dir.create(results_dir, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

## Subset to Cardiomyocytes

Cardiomyocytes carry the foetal→adult maturation signal we want to
trace. Running pseudotime on all cell types at once would mix several
biological processes into one trajectory.

```{r subset-cm}
cm <- query[, query$PhiCellTypeBroad == "Cardiomyocyte"]
cat("Cardiomyocytes:", ncol(cm), "\n")
print(table(cm$group))
print(sort(table(cm$PhiCellType), decreasing = TRUE))
```

The fine Φ-Space labels (`Cardiomyocyte:Fetal_enriched_*`,
`:Metabolic`, `:Stressed`, …) split the cardiomyocytes into
biologically meaningful subtypes. We'll use them as slingshot's clusters.

## A Map for Plotting: PCA and UMAP

To display pseudotimes we need a 2D map of the cells. We compute a
standard pipeline on the logcounts: highly variable genes, then PCA,
then UMAP. None of the pseudotime methods below uses the UMAP; it is
only for plotting, so that every method is drawn on the same layout.

```{r pca-expression}
pca_cache <- file.path(results_dir, "06_cm_pca.rds")

if (file.exists(pca_cache)) {
    cm <- readRDS(pca_cache)
    message("Loaded cached CM object with PCA from ", pca_cache)
} else {
    # Highly variable gene selection
    gene_var <- rowVars(as.matrix(logcounts(cm)))
    names(gene_var) <- rownames(cm)
    n_hvg <- min(2000, nrow(cm))
    hvg <- names(sort(gene_var, decreasing = TRUE))[seq_len(n_hvg)]

    pca <- prcomp(t(as.matrix(logcounts(cm)[hvg, ])),
                  center = TRUE, scale. = FALSE)
    reducedDim(cm, "PCA") <- pca$x[, 1:20]
    saveRDS(cm, pca_cache)
}

cat("PCA dims:      ", paste(dim(reducedDim(cm, "PCA")), collapse = " x "), "\n")
cat("PhiSpace dims: ", paste(dim(reducedDim(cm, "PhiSpace")),
                             collapse = " x "), "\n")
```

We keep the first 20 principal components.

`n_neighbors = 15` and `min_dist = 0.5` were chosen by trying several
settings: smaller `n_neighbors` broke the cardiomyocyte continuum into
islands with no biological meaning.

```{r umap}
umap_cache <- file.path(results_dir, "06_cm_umap.rds")

if (file.exists(umap_cache)) {
    reducedDim(cm, "UMAP") <- readRDS(umap_cache)
    message("Loaded cached UMAP")
} else {
    set.seed(42)
    cm <- scater::runUMAP(cm, dimred = "PCA", name = "UMAP",
                          n_neighbors = 15, min_dist = 0.5)
    saveRDS(reducedDim(cm, "UMAP"), umap_cache)
}
```

A few small helpers for the plots and runs below:

```{r helpers}
umap_df <- as.data.frame(reducedDim(cm, "UMAP"))
colnames(umap_df) <- c("UMAP1", "UMAP2")

# Rescale to [0, 1] so different methods share one colour scale
rescale01 <- function(x) {
    x <- x - min(x, na.rm = TRUE)
    x / max(x, na.rm = TRUE)
}

# UMAP coloured by a pseudotime (blue = early, red = late)
umap_base <- function(pt_vec) {
    ggplot(cbind(umap_df, pt = pt_vec), aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = pt)) +
        geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.7) +
        scale_colour_distiller(palette = "Spectral", name = "Pseudotime") +
        theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
        theme(aspect.ratio = 1)
}

# Slingshot curves, re-fitted in UMAP space for display
embed_curves_df <- function(sds, label) {
    curves <- slingCurves(embedCurves(sds, reducedDim(cm, "UMAP")))
    do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_along(curves), function(i) {
        s <- curves[[i]]$s[curves[[i]]$ord, , drop = FALSE]
        data.frame(UMAP1 = s[, 1], UMAP2 = s[, 2],
                   lineage = paste0(label, "_L", i))
    }))
}
with_curves <- function(p, crv_df) {
    p + geom_path(data = crv_df, aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, group = lineage),
                  inherit.aes = FALSE, colour = "grey30", linewidth = 0.8)
}

# Run slingshot, or load a cached run
run_slingshot <- function(cache, dimred, clusters, start) {
    fp <- file.path(results_dir, cache)
    if (file.exists(fp)) {
        message("Loaded cached ", cache)
        return(readRDS(fp))
    }
    sds <- slingshot(
        reducedDim(cm, dimred),
        clusterLabels = clusters,
        start.clus    = start,
        dist.method   = "simple"
    )
    saveRDS(sds, fp)
    sds
}

# One pseudotime per cell: the mean over slingshot's lineages
lineage_pt <- function(sds) rowMeans(slingPseudotime(sds), na.rm = TRUE)
```

`dist.method = "simple"` is needed because slingshot's default distance
fails when some clusters are very small.

## Pseudotime 1: the Φ-Space Score

The simplest ordering needs no trajectory model. The reference has four
age groups (`fetal`, `young`, `middle`, `old`). We average the three
post-natal scores into an "adult" score and subtract the `fetal` score:

$$\text{Φ-Space pseudotime} = \text{mean}(\text{young}, \text{middle}, \text{old}) - \text{fetal}$$

The raw difference has long tails, which squash the colour scale, so for
display we also show a cube-root version (`sign(x) · |x|^(1/3)`). It
compresses the tails without changing the order of cells.

```{r phi-pseudotime, fig.width=13, fig.height=11}
phi_scores     <- reducedDim(cm, "PhiSpace")
adult_score    <- rowMeans(phi_scores[, c("young", "middle", "old")])
cm$fetal_score <- phi_scores[, "fetal"]
cm$pt_phi_score    <- adult_score - cm$fetal_score
cm$pt_phi_score_cr <- sign(cm$pt_phi_score) * abs(cm$pt_phi_score)^(1/3)

p_group <- ggplot(cbind(umap_df, group = cm$group),
                  aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = group)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 3))) +
    labs(title = "Donor stage", colour = "Stage")

p_fetal <- ggplot(cbind(umap_df, fetal = cm$fetal_score),
                  aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = fetal)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_gradient(low = "white", high = "blue") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) + theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
    labs(title = "Φ-Space fetal score", colour = "fetal")

p_phi    <- umap_base(cm$pt_phi_score) +
    labs(title = "Φ-Space pseudotime (adult − fetal)")
p_phi_cr <- umap_base(cm$pt_phi_score_cr) +
    labs(title = "Φ-Space pseudotime (cube-root, for display)")

(p_group | p_fetal) / (p_phi | p_phi_cr)
```

The gradient from foetal to adult donors (top left) is matched by the
Φ-Space pseudotime (bottom row). This is the baseline the fitted methods
should reproduce: if they don't, something has gone wrong.

## Pseudotime 2: Slingshot

Slingshot needs a **starting cluster**. We pick the cardiomyocyte subtype
with the highest mean `fetal` score: Φ-Space sets the direction, and the
clusters define the units the tree is built from.

```{r pick-anchor}
mean_fetal_by <- function(cluster_vec) {
    tibble(cluster = cluster_vec, fetal = cm$fetal_score) |>
        group_by(cluster) |>
        summarise(mean_fetal = mean(fetal), n = n(), .groups = "drop") |>
        arrange(desc(mean_fetal))
}

anchor_phict_tbl <- mean_fetal_by(cm$PhiCellType)
anchor_phict_tbl
start_cluster_phict <- as.character(anchor_phict_tbl$cluster[1])
cat("start.clus:", start_cluster_phict, "\n")
```

```{r slingshot-phi}
sling_phi_phict <- run_slingshot("06_slingshot_phi_phict.rds",
                                 "PhiSpace", cm$PhiCellType,
                                 start_cluster_phict)
cm$pt_sling_phi_phict <- lineage_pt(sling_phi_phict)
cat("Lineages found:", length(slingLineages(sling_phi_phict)), "\n")
```

`slingPseudotime()` returns one column per lineage; we average them to
get one pseudotime per cell.

```{r slingshot-umap, fig.width=7, fig.height=6}
curves_phi_phict_df <- embed_curves_df(sling_phi_phict, "phi_phict")
with_curves(umap_base(rescale01(cm$pt_sling_phi_phict)),
            curves_phi_phict_df) +
    labs(title = "Slingshot pseudotime, with its principal curve")
```

## Pseudotime 3: Diffusion Pseudotime (DPT)

DPT needs a single **root cell**. We take the cell with the highest
`fetal` score.

```{r root-cell}
root_cell <- which.max(cm$fetal_score)
cat("Root cell index:", root_cell,
    " (fetal score =", round(cm$fetal_score[root_cell], 3), ")\n")
```

```{r destiny-dpt-phi}
dpt_phi_cache <- file.path(results_dir, "06_dpt_phispace.rds")

if (file.exists(dpt_phi_cache)) {
    dpt_phi <- readRDS(dpt_phi_cache)
    message("Loaded cached DPT/PhiSpace result")
} else {
    dm_phi <- DiffusionMap(as.matrix(reducedDim(cm, "PhiSpace")),
                           n_eigs = 20, sigma = "local",
                           verbose = FALSE)
    dpt_phi <- DPT(dm_phi, tips = root_cell)
    saveRDS(dpt_phi, dpt_phi_cache)
}

cm$pt_dpt_phi <- dpt_phi$dpt
summary(cm$pt_dpt_phi)
```

Without `tips`, destiny would pick end points itself. We set the root
explicitly so that DPT starts from the same place as the other two
pseudotimes.

## Do the Three Pseudotimes Agree?

<!-- The point is that in reality we need to try a few methods to see which one makes sense. This section provides some ways for benchmarking. -->

### On the UMAP

```{r compare-umap, fig.width=15, fig.height=5.5}
cm$pt_phi_score_01       <- rescale01(cm$pt_phi_score_cr)
cm$pt_sling_phi_phict_01 <- rescale01(cm$pt_sling_phi_phict)
cm$pt_dpt_phi_01         <- rescale01(cm$pt_dpt_phi)

# `+` binds tighter than `|` and `/`, so wrap the whole layout before
# adding plot_layout(); otherwise it applies to the last panel only.
((umap_base(cm$pt_phi_score_01) + labs(title = "Φ-Space score")) |
    (with_curves(umap_base(cm$pt_sling_phi_phict_01), curves_phi_phict_df) +
         labs(title = "Slingshot")) |
    (umap_base(cm$pt_dpt_phi_01) + labs(title = "DPT"))) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect")
```

### By rank correlation

Each method has its own scale, and only the *order* of cells matters, so
we compare them with Spearman (rank) correlation.

```{r compare-cor}
pt_mat <- data.frame(
    `Φ-Space score` = cm$pt_phi_score,
    Slingshot       = cm$pt_sling_phi_phict,
    DPT             = cm$pt_dpt_phi,
    check.names = FALSE
)
round(cor(pt_mat, use = "complete.obs", method = "spearman"), 3)
```

The correlations are positive but well below 1: the three methods agree
on the broad order, not on the details.

### Against donor stage

The donors' stage is **held-out information**: no method saw it. If a
pseudotime captures maturation, its values should rise from foetal to
young to adult donors.

```{r compare-stage, fig.width=11, fig.height=4}
stage_df <- pt_mat |>
    mutate(group = factor(cm$group, levels = c("fetal", "young", "adult"))) |>
    tidyr::pivot_longer(-group, names_to = "method", values_to = "pseudotime") |>
    group_by(method) |>
    mutate(pseudotime = rescale01(pseudotime),
           method = factor(method, levels = colnames(pt_mat)))

ggplot(stage_df, aes(group, pseudotime, fill = group)) +
    geom_violin(scale = "width", alpha = 0.8) +
    geom_boxplot(width = 0.15, alpha = 0.6, outlier.size = 0.3) +
    scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
    facet_wrap(~ method, nrow = 1) +
    labs(x = "Donor stage", y = "Pseudotime (rescaled)",
         title = "Do the pseudotimes recover the foetal → adult order?") +
    theme_bw(base_size = 12) +
    theme(legend.position = "none")
```

What the plot shows:

- **All three put foetal nuclei clearly first.** The biggest change in
  this data is between the foetal and the post-natal heart.
- **None separates young from adult donors well.** Within the post-natal
  heart, maturity varies about as much within an age group as between
  them.
- **DPT is nearly all-or-nothing:** foetal nuclei sit near 0 and almost
  all post-natal nuclei near 1. It orders the foetal-to-post-natal
  transition but says little about differences after birth.

The spread *within* each stage shows how much nuclei from donors of the
same age differ, which is exactly what a single age label hides.

## A Pitfall: Slingshot Depends on the Clustering

<!-- Make this an extension part: ask participants to think about the effect of clustering on slingshot and then ask them to run the code. Also mark this part optional, as we might need to skip this part. -->

Slingshot builds its tree on **cluster centres**, so the clustering you
give it is a modelling choice, not a preprocessing detail. To see how
much it matters, we rerun slingshot with:

- a different **clustering:** standard unsupervised (Louvain) clusters
  on the PCA embedding, which know nothing about the reference;
- a different **embedding:** PCA of gene expression instead of the
  Φ-Space scores.

That gives four slingshot runs (2 clusterings × 2 embeddings), all
started from the most foetal cluster.

```{r sensitivity-runs}
# Unsupervised clustering: SNN graph on the PCA embedding, Louvain
cluster_cache <- file.path(results_dir, "06_cm_clusters.rds")
if (file.exists(cluster_cache)) {
    cm$cluster <- readRDS(cluster_cache)
    message("Loaded cached clusters")
} else {
    set.seed(42)
    snn <- scran::buildSNNGraph(cm, use.dimred = "PCA", k = 20)
    cm$cluster <- factor(igraph::cluster_louvain(snn)$membership)
    saveRDS(cm$cluster, cluster_cache)
}
start_cluster_unsup <- as.character(mean_fetal_by(cm$cluster)$cluster[1])

sling_phi_unsup <- run_slingshot("06_slingshot_phi_unsup.rds",
                                 "PhiSpace", cm$cluster, start_cluster_unsup)
sling_pca_unsup <- run_slingshot("06_slingshot_pca_unsup.rds",
                                 "PCA",      cm$cluster, start_cluster_unsup)
sling_pca_phict <- run_slingshot("06_slingshot_pca_phict.rds",
                                 "PCA",      cm$PhiCellType, start_cluster_phict)

cm$pt_sling_phi_unsup <- lineage_pt(sling_phi_unsup)
cm$pt_sling_pca_unsup <- lineage_pt(sling_pca_unsup)
cm$pt_sling_pca_phict <- lineage_pt(sling_pca_phict)
```

```{r sensitivity-figure, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
curves_phi_unsup_df <- embed_curves_df(sling_phi_unsup, "phi_unsup")
curves_pca_unsup_df <- embed_curves_df(sling_pca_unsup, "pca_unsup")
curves_pca_phict_df <- embed_curves_df(sling_pca_phict, "pca_phict")

p_phi_unsup <- with_curves(umap_base(rescale01(cm$pt_sling_phi_unsup)),
                           curves_phi_unsup_df) +
    labs(title = "Φ-Space / unsupervised clusters")
p_pca_unsup <- with_curves(umap_base(rescale01(cm$pt_sling_pca_unsup)),
                           curves_pca_unsup_df) +
    labs(title = "PCA / unsupervised clusters")
p_phi_phict <- with_curves(umap_base(cm$pt_sling_phi_phict_01),
                           curves_phi_phict_df) +
    labs(title = "Φ-Space / Φ-Space cell types (used above)")
p_pca_phict <- with_curves(umap_base(rescale01(cm$pt_sling_pca_phict)),
                           curves_pca_phict_df) +
    labs(title = "PCA / Φ-Space cell types")

((p_phi_unsup | p_pca_unsup) / (p_phi_phict | p_pca_phict)) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(
        title    = "Slingshot with two clusterings × two embeddings",
        subtitle = "Top: unsupervised Louvain clusters. Bottom: Φ-Space cell types from Module 1."
    )
```

Two numbers per run make the comparison concrete: how many lineages
(branches) slingshot found, and how well the pseudotime agrees with donor
stage.

```{r sensitivity-table}
stage_num <- as.numeric(factor(cm$group, levels = c("fetal", "young", "adult")))
sling_runs <- list(
    "Φ-Space / unsupervised"       = sling_phi_unsup,
    "PCA / unsupervised"           = sling_pca_unsup,
    "Φ-Space / Φ-Space cell types" = sling_phi_phict,
    "PCA / Φ-Space cell types"     = sling_pca_phict
)
tibble(
    run       = names(sling_runs),
    lineages  = vapply(sling_runs, function(s) length(slingLineages(s)), integer(1)),
    spearman_vs_stage = vapply(sling_runs, function(s)
        round(cor(lineage_pt(s), stage_num, method = "spearman"), 2), numeric(1))
)
```

Reading the figure and the table:

- **The clustering changes the shape of the trajectory.** With the
  unsupervised clusters, slingshot builds a branching tree with many
  lineages; with the Φ-Space cell types, it finds only a few. The curves,
  and therefore what "pseudotime" means for a given cell, differ visibly.
- **Yet all four runs agree with donor stage about equally.** A single
  summary check like this can look fine even when the trajectories
  disagree.

The lesson: **don't trust one trajectory or one check.** Look at the
structure of the trajectory itself, compare it with independent
information such as donor age, and compare it with a method that does not
need a clustering, such as DPT.

## Handing Off to Module 3

We save the cardiomyocytes, with their UMAP and pseudotimes, for
Module 3.

```{r save-for-module3}
final_cache <- file.path(results_dir, "06_cm_pseudotime.rds")
saveRDS(cm, final_cache)
cat("Annotated CM object at", final_cache, "\n")
```

In addition to everything Module 1 handed over, the object carries:

- `reducedDim(cm, "PCA")` and `reducedDim(cm, "UMAP")`;
- `pt_phi_score`, the Φ-Space pseudotime (`adult − fetal`);
- `pt_sling_phi_phict` and `pt_dpt_phi`, the slingshot and DPT
  pseudotimes on Φ-Space;
- `cluster` and the three other slingshot runs from the sensitivity
  figure;
- `*_01` columns: pseudotimes rescaled to `[0, 1]`.

Module 3 uses `pt_phi_score` to pick genes associated with maturation:
it needs no trajectory model, so Module 3 does not depend on the
slingshot or DPT choices above.

## Summary

- Pseudotime orders cells along a process. It is not real time, and
  some methods need to be told where the process starts.
- We built three orderings of the cardiomyocytes: the Φ-Space score (no
  model), slingshot (principal curve) and DPT (diffusion). All three put
  foetal nuclei first; none separates young from adult donors well.
- The clustering given to slingshot changes the shape of the trajectory
  (how many branches), even when its agreement with donor age barely
  changes. Look at the trajectory itself, and compare it with independent
  information and with a different method.

## Going Further (Optional)

This section is not needed for Module 3. It repeats the comparison with
a second embedding: **PCA of gene expression** instead of the Φ-Space
scores. Crossing two methods (slingshot, DPT) with two embeddings
(Φ-Space, PCA) separates the effect of the method from the effect of the
embedding.

### DPT on PCA

Same settings and root cell as before; only the embedding changes.

```{r destiny-dpt-pca}
dpt_cache <- file.path(results_dir, "06_dpt_pca.rds")

if (file.exists(dpt_cache)) {
    dpt <- readRDS(dpt_cache)
    message("Loaded cached DPT/PCA result")
} else {
    dm  <- DiffusionMap(as.matrix(reducedDim(cm, "PCA")),
                        n_eigs = 20, sigma = "local", verbose = FALSE)
    dpt <- DPT(dm, tips = root_cell)
    saveRDS(dpt, dpt_cache)
}

cm$pt_dpt_pca <- dpt$dpt
summary(cm$pt_dpt_pca)
```

### Two methods × two embeddings

```{r umap-pt-plots, fig.width=12, fig.height=10}
p_sling_phi <- with_curves(umap_base(cm$pt_sling_phi_phict_01),
                           curves_phi_phict_df) +
    labs(title = "slingshot / Φ-Space")
p_sling_pca <- with_curves(umap_base(rescale01(cm$pt_sling_pca_phict)),
                           curves_pca_phict_df) +
    labs(title = "slingshot / PCA")
p_dpt_phi <- umap_base(cm$pt_dpt_phi_01) + labs(title = "DPT / Φ-Space")
p_dpt_pca <- umap_base(rescale01(cm$pt_dpt_pca)) + labs(title = "DPT / PCA")

((p_sling_phi | p_sling_pca) / (p_dpt_phi | p_dpt_pca)) +
    plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
    plot_annotation(title = "Pseudotime on UMAP: two methods × two embeddings")
```

If all four panels show the same blue → red gradient over the same UMAP
regions, the trajectory is robust. If the two slingshot panels agree
with each other but not with the DPT panels, that is a *method* effect;
if the two Φ-Space panels agree but the two PCA panels do not, it is an
*embedding* effect.

### Correlations and pairwise agreement

```{r pt-cor}
pt_mat4 <- data.frame(
    `slingshot/PhiSpace` = cm$pt_sling_phi_phict,
    `slingshot/PCA`      = cm$pt_sling_pca_phict,
    `DPT/PhiSpace`       = cm$pt_dpt_phi,
    `DPT/PCA`            = cm$pt_dpt_pca,
    check.names = FALSE
)
round(cor(pt_mat4, use = "complete.obs", method = "spearman"), 3)
```

```{r pt-pairs, fig.width=10, fig.height=7}
pt_long <- as.data.frame(lapply(pt_mat4, rescale01), check.names = FALSE) |>
    mutate(group = cm$group)

make_pair <- function(x, y) {
    ggplot(pt_long, aes(.data[[x]], .data[[y]], colour = group)) +
        geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.5) +
        geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, linetype = "dashed", alpha = 0.5) +
        scale_colour_brewer(palette = "Set1") +
        theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
        theme(legend.position = "none") +
        labs(x = x, y = y)
}

pairs <- lapply(combn(colnames(pt_mat4), 2, simplify = FALSE),
                function(p) make_pair(p[1], p[2]))
wrap_plots(pairs, ncol = 3) +
    plot_annotation(title = "Pairwise agreement between pseudotimes (coloured by donor stage)")
```

How to read the pairs:

- **Same method, different embedding** (slingshot/PhiSpace vs
  slingshot/PCA; DPT/PhiSpace vs DPT/PCA): the embedding effect.
- **Same embedding, different method** (slingshot vs DPT on Φ-Space; on
  PCA): the method effect.
- **Both different** (slingshot/PhiSpace vs DPT/PCA; slingshot/PCA vs
  DPT/PhiSpace): agreement here is the strongest evidence that the
  ordering is not an artefact of either choice.

### The unsupervised clusters

The Louvain clusters used in the sensitivity figure, for reference:

```{r umap-clusters, fig.width=7, fig.height=5.5}
clust_levels <- levels(cm$cluster)
clust_pal <- c(brewer.pal(9, "Set1"), brewer.pal(8, "Dark2"),
               brewer.pal(8, "Set2"))[seq_along(clust_levels)]
names(clust_pal) <- clust_levels

ggplot(cbind(umap_df, cluster = cm$cluster),
       aes(UMAP1, UMAP2, colour = cluster)) +
    geom_point(size = 0.4, alpha = 0.7) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = clust_pal) +
    theme_bw(base_size = 11) +
    theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(override.aes = list(size = 2))) +
    labs(title = "Unsupervised Louvain clusters (SNN on PCA)")
```
